The same 1 March date is the priority deadline for master admission; the master application web closes 1 August and applicants from outside the EU who do not reside in Norway must apply by 15 June for residence-permit timing.
official.status_note: The official scholarship page is live (updated 6 October 2026) and describes an annual round: BI's admission portal for full-time programmes opens 1 November, the master scholarship deadline is 1 March, and decisions are communicated by the end of April.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Scholarships will cover full tuition fees for up to two years of study in a full-time master's degree.

official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open to candidates admitted to the first year of a full-time master's degree at campus Oslo, campus Bergen or campus Trondheim; applicants to the BI-Luiss Joint Masters in Marketing are not eligible

official.description: BI Norwegian Business School, a member of the GBSN Network and a participant in GMAC's Study in Europe Initiative and the SEED Business School Festival in Africa, offers two scholarships to support these initiatives specifically in Africa. The scholarship covers full tuition fees for up to two years of a full-time master's degree and a stipend for living expenses of NOK 50,000 per semester, if the student achieves the academic progression requirements. Awards are made on academic merit, not financial need, and recipients act as BI Ambassadors.
official.program_type: Entrance scholarship for full-time master's studies, awarded on academic merit
official.english_requirement: For applicants whose first language is not English, a minimum of IELTS Academic overall 6.5, TOEFL iBT overall 90, Pearson PTE Academic overall 62, Cambridge C1 Advanced (CAE) overall 176 or C2 Proficiency (CPE) overall 180. A waiver may be requested for native English speakers or applicants who have completed two or more academic years of study where the language of instruction was English. BI states that an English aptitude test (as well as the GMAT/GRE) must be taken before 1 March for an applicant to be considered for a scholarship.

applicant_utility.summary: BI awards two Future African Leader Scholarships a year to African citizens entering the first year of a full-time MSc at its Oslo, Bergen or Trondheim campuses, covering full tuition for up to two years plus NOK 50,000 per semester. With only two awards and an explicitly merit-based process, you are competing against BI's entire African applicant pool on grades and test scores, so a 4.0 ECTS GPA plus a strong GMAT or GRE is the entry ticket rather than a differentiator. One useful quirk: the same single one-page letter automatically puts you in contention for BI's Presidential, Master International and Women in Finance and Tech scholarships, so there is no extra work in applying for those too. Be realistic about the stipend - it is roughly NOK 100,000 per year against BI's own estimated living expenses of about NOK 152,000, so you need a credible plan for the gap.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A recent African graduate of a GBSN member school (or an attendee of a GMAC Study in Europe or SEED Business School Festival event in Africa) with a 4.0+ ECTS GPA and GMAT/GRE and English scores already in hand before 1 March.
application_readiness_checklist: Sit the GMAT or GRE and an IELTS/TOEFL/PTE/Cambridge English test before 1 March - BI states scholarship applicants without those scores are not considered for a scholarship

Check your bachelor record against BI's ECTS conversion: the scholarship threshold is 4.0 on that scale, well above the 3.50 admission minimum, and BI will convert international grades itself, so make sure your transcript includes the official grading scale
Draft one single PDF containing a one-page CV and a scholarship letter of at most one page that names your GBSN member school, or the GMAC/SEED event with its date and place

Submit the admission application and the scholarship upload in the same portal session, then accept the admission offer as soon as it arrives - the scholarship file is only assessed for accepted offers
Prepare the same upload set with BI's financial declaration template, passport copy and certified English translations of diplomas and transcripts
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 1 March scholarship cut-off: late applications are explicitly not considered even though admission itself stays open until 1 August
Applying without a verified GMAT/GRE and English test in hand - BI warns this removes you from scholarship consideration and even blocks a conditional offer
Being a Norway resident, or holding Norwegian/Nordic credits that make you a domestic applicant, or applying to the BI-Luiss Joint Masters in Marketing, which is excluded
Already holding a master's degree - only first-time master's applicants are considered for full-time master scholarships
A letter full of generalities that never names the GBSN school or the GMAC/SEED event that triggers the preference
Losing the award after enrolment by falling below 30 ECTS progression, dropping under a cumulative 'B', or recording a failing grade
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: BI lists 2026-27 external non-EU/EEA MSc tuition at NOK 166,700 per year and its own estimated living expenses at NOK 151,690 per year; the stipend provides about NOK 100,000 per year, so plan on roughly NOK 50,000 or more per year of living costs, plus flights, a housing deposit, travel and insurance, course literature, excursions and any re-sit fees (NOK 330 per ECTS), none of which the scholarship covers.
document_audit: Everything goes into one PDF under 25 MB (pdf, jpg, jpeg or png) - CV, letter, transcripts, test scores, passport and financial declaration cannot be drip-fed later
Paper diplomas only: BI rejects electronic diplomas and returns the application, so scan the original document
If your passport name differs from your diploma name, a name-change certificate from the Norwegian Tax Administration is mandatory
Transcripts must include an official explanation of the grading scale, in English or as a certified translation alongside the original
Send GMAT/GRE and TOEFL results directly from the providers (GRE institution code 0497, TOEFL code 0529) or upload the score report; IELTS copies are only accepted when the TRF number is visible
Nothing can be added after submission - BI accepts no additional documentation once the application is in
alerts: BI's own warning is blunt: academically strong master applicants far outnumber available scholarships, and only two awards exist here - treat it as a reach award and keep a funding plan B
Only one scholarship per applicant is awarded, so apply for several BI scholarships with the same letter but do not assume awards can be stacked
The award is tied to one specific master's programme and campus and cannot be transferred if you switch programme
Scholarship offers must be accepted by the date on the offer, otherwise they are withdrawn and given to another candidate
Decisions come near the end of April, after the admission offer, and are final with no appeal route
Candidates eligible for Norwegian tuition reduction or a Lånekassen loan are treated as domestic applicants and are outside this scholarship's scope
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create one application in BI's online admission portal, upload the admission documents plus the combined CV and one-page scholarship letter into the 'Scholarship' section, submit before 1 March, then accept the admission offer and wait for the end-of-April decision.
